quotes.text: A pipeline is a logical grouping of activities that together do one unit of work. That's Microsoft's definition, and it translates to something simple.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Gives the core definition of a pipeline in plain words.

quotes.text: The linked service is the key and the address of the building. The data set is the exact mailbox inside. You need both before you can deliver anything
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A clear image that resolves the most common beginner confusion between linked services and datasets.

quotes.text: The schedule trigger starts a run and moves on while the tumbling window waits for that run to finish and reports back on whether it worked.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains the practical difference between two trigger types in one sentence.

quotes.text: Turn on retries and aim to make your work idempotent, which is a ten dollar word for a simple idea. Idempotent means safe to run twice without duplicating your data.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A concrete best practice for reliable data pipelines, explained simply.

quotes.text: Build a single pipeline with one copy activity and prove the path works from end to end before you add anything clever. A boring pipeline that runs beats a clever one that half works.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A memorable recommendation to start simple.

takeaways: Azure Data Factory orchestrates data movement and transformation with pipelines of activities, linked services as connections, datasets as pointers, integration runtimes as compute and triggers as start signals.
Mapping data flows let you transform data without code on managed Spark clusters, but they cost more than simple copies because each run starts at eight cores.
Microsoft now points newcomers to Data Factory in Microsoft Fabric, and the pipeline and activity model transfers between both platforms.
hook: Company data is scattered across databases, spreadsheets and file shares, and moving it into reports by hand or with custom code is slow and fragile. This beginner-friendly episode explains Azure Data Factory's building blocks, triggers, data flows, costs and how it compares with Data Factory in Microsoft Fabric. Analysts, admins and aspiring data engineers will be able to explain the tool and decide where to start learning.
